roll_call: I was the 18th president of the Republic of Korea and its first woman president. My term began in 2013 and ended with my removal in 2017.
I studied electronic engineering, served five terms in the National Assembly, and was then elected president.
I was known as President Park Chung-hee's daughter and entered politics as a lawmaker in 1998. The responsibility of the presidency remains under my own name.
deploy: Break down the boundaries between science, technology, and culture to create new markets and jobs. That was the idea I called the creative economy.
Correct unfair practices so that large companies and small businesses can grow together.
Respond firmly to North Korean provocations, but do not use politics as an excuse to ignore the pain of separated families.
battle_win: The people elected the Republic of Korea's first woman president. That record belongs more to a change in our politics than to me alone.
We established seventeen Centers for Creative Economy and Innovation nationwide. We tried to build a path from ideas to startups and jobs.
In 2015, the two Koreas agreed to ease tensions and continue official talks and reunions for separated families.
battle_draw: I chose pressure by fully shutting down the Kaesong Industrial Complex. It was intended to protect security, but it also severed the last inter-Korean link.
We overhauled the safety system after the Sewol ferry disaster, but no institutional reform could restore the lives lost in the failed rescue.
I made the creative economy and cultural enrichment pillars of my administration, but the end of my term was recorded not by policy achievements but by a constitutional judgment.
battle_lose: In the Sewol ferry disaster, the state failed to save its people. As president, I bore the ultimate responsibility for that disaster.
The Constitutional Court ruled that my conduct betrayed the people's trust, and I was removed from the presidency.
The Supreme Court finalized a twenty-year sentence in the state-affairs corruption case. That judgment weighs more heavily than my time in office.
clash_attack: Do not mix public authority with private trust. Presidential judgment must rest on official procedures and records.
Do not lose sight of public safety while speaking of national security. The state must move first in a disaster.
Look at results, not the name of a policy. If people's lives do not improve, a slogan cannot make the policy complete.

roll_call: I was South Korea's first woman president, and I was removed from office in 2017.
I studied engineering, served five terms in the National Assembly, and became president.
I was known as Park Chung-hee's daughter, but presidential responsibility was mine.
deploy: Combine science, technology, and culture to create new jobs.
Stop unfair deals by conglomerates so smaller companies can grow too.
Prepare for North Korean provocations, but keep separated families connected.
battle_win: For the first time, South Koreans elected a woman president.
We established seventeen Creative Economy Innovation Centers nationwide.
In 2015, the two Koreas agreed to talks and family reunions.
battle_draw: Closing Kaesong pressured North Korea, but it also severed our last connection.
We reformed safety after Sewol, but no reform can restore the lives lost.
I promoted the creative economy, but my term ended with removal from office.
battle_lose: During the Sewol disaster, the state failed its people. As president, I was responsible.
The Constitutional Court removed me for betraying the people's trust.
The Supreme Court upheld my twenty-year sentence in the corruption case.
clash_attack: Never mix presidential power with private relationships!
Save the people before invoking national security!
Forget the policy name. Look at people's lives!

roll_call: I won the U.S. Women's Open at nineteen, then captured the first three majors of the 2013 season in succession.
I completed the career Grand Slam in 2015 and won Olympic gold in Rio in 2016.
I became known more for my putting than my driving. Consistent pace and distance control are at the heart of my game.
deploy: Do not look only at the flag. First choose the miss that leaves the easiest next shot.
A round with missed chances is better than one with no chances at all. Read the next putt again.
Treat even a four-shot lead as if it were gone. At a major, one hole can change the entire round.
battle_win: I went to Rio with an injured thumb and finished four rounds to win gold by five strokes.
I won the first three majors of the 2013 season. It was an honor to put my name in the history of women's golf.
I completed the career Grand Slam and reached the Hall of Fame. The years of endurance matter as much as the victories.
battle_draw: Years of missing greens taught me to recover from anywhere. That weakness built the putting game I became known for.
Some days putts finish short, long, or to either side. Golf does not always turn good shots into scores.
The lead is an advantage, but it brings pressure. Composure means keeping the same routine within that pressure, not escaping it.
battle_lose: After my first major in 2008, I went eighty-one LPGA starts without another victory. Even after reaching the top, I endured a long silence.
My 2013 season Grand Slam ended at St Andrews. Winning three majors did not guarantee a fourth.
A thumb injury ended my 2016 LPGA season. The body's warning must come before the record book.
clash_attack: Do not measure me by distance alone. The player who saves the ball and takes one fewer stroke finishes ahead.
My swing may look slow, but the rhythm is mine. I trust a motion I can repeat over one that merely looks good.
Do not avoid the leaderboard. Watching the scores gave me motivation to stay in front.

Putting made my name, not driving. I trust pace and distance control.
deploy: Do not chase the flag. Miss where the next shot stays easy.

battle_win: I reached Rio with an injured thumb and won gold by five strokes.
I won the first three majors of 2013. I still treasure that honor.
I earned a career Grand Slam and the Hall of Fame. The endurance paid off.
battle_draw: Missing greens taught me the short game, and that sharpened my putting.
Some days the putts just won't drop. Even good shots do not always lower the score.

clash_attack: Distance isn't everything. Saving one stroke is!
